item.title: Oil production rises 6.2% to 1.615m bpd, Dangote supply jumps 25%
item.description: •Pipeline outages, terminal delays hamper output By Ediri Ejoh Nigeria’s average daily crude oil and condensate production rose by 6.2 per cent to 1.615 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025, from 1.521 million bpd in 2024, while crude oil supplied to Dangote Refinery increased by 25.3 per cent to 94.44 million barrels. The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) disclosed this in its 2025 Financial and Operational Performance Report, released at the weekend. The report showed that crude oil production, excluding condensates, increased by 12.6 per cent to 1.475 million bpd in 2025, from 1.310 million bpd in the preceding year. Companies operating under Joint Venture (JV) arrangements and those in land terrains accounted for the largest shares of national production. A breakdown of monthly output showed that production peaked at 1.701 million bpd in July and 1.688 million bpd in June, while the lowest output of 1.521 million bpd was recorded in December. Providing details of production performance, the commission stated: “Reconciled crude oil produced was 589,600,527 barrels (538,696,941 barrels of oil and 50,903,586 barrels of condensate). The daily average production figure was 1,615,344 barrels per day (1,475,882 barrels of oil per day and 139,462 barrels of condensate per day).” It also disclosed that 48 Field Development Plans (FDPs) were approved during the year to develop about 1,751.15 million stock tank barrels of oil reserves, 104.48 million stock tank barrels of condensate reserves and 8.19 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves. However, pipeline outages, planned maintenance and terminal operational challenges constrained production during the year. The commission identified the Trans-Niger Pipeline (TNP), Nembe Creek Trunk Line (NCTL) and Trans Forcados Pipeline (TFP) among the major pipelines affected by outages. “The most prevalent cause during the year was outages of key pipelines (TNP, NCTL, and TFP),” the report stated. It added that “planned maintenance and vessel/tanker loading delays at terminals, which led to the shut-in of wells, also contributed significantly to the deferred volumes.” Meanwhile, crude oil supplied to Dangote Refinery rose to 94.436 million barrels in 2025, from 75.391 million barrels in 2024, representing an increase of 25.3 per cent. In a related development, the NUPRC last week reported that Nigeria’s average daily crude oil and condensate production declined by 1.7 per cent to 1.68 million bpd in October 2026, from 1.71 million bpd in September. Despite the decline, Nigeria met its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) crude oil production quota for the sixth consecutive month. Crude oil output, excluding condensates, averaged 1.51 million bpd, representing 101 per cent of the country’s 1.5 million bpd quota. item.title: APC shuts down Umuahia for Tinubu
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The All Progressives Congress, APC, on Monday, shut down Umuahia, the Abia State capital, as it formally flagged off its campaign for the 2027 general elections, with a massive rally that drew party leaders, candidates and supporters from across the state. The Umuahia Township Stadium, venue of the rally, was filled to capacity, while heavy vehicular and human traffic disrupted movement around adjoining streets as thousands of party faithful struggled to access the venue. Leading the charge, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, declared that Abia would deliver 75 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in 2027, insisting that the President would not have to beg for the constitutionally required 25 per cent in the state. Kalu said APC had about 162,000 members in Abia and that the party had challenged each member to mobilise 10 additional voters for Tinubu. According to him, such mobilisation would translate into over 1.6 million votes for the President. “Don’t beg for 25 per cent. Your sons and daughters in Abia State will give you 75 per cent. We have about 2.3 million voters in Abia State. We are mobilising. We are not sleeping,” he declared. He challenged those questioning APC’s electoral strength in Abia to wait for the party’s planned rally at Enyimba Stadium, Aba, on December 7, insisting that the Umuahia rally, organised within one week, was only a foretaste of what was coming. Tinubu has remembered South-East — Kalu Explaining why the South-East should support Tinubu’s second-term ambition, Kalu listed the establishment of the South-East Development Commission, stabilisation of the foreign exchange market, student loans under NELFUND, tax reforms and increased security funding among the administration’s achievements. He said the President had demonstrated commitment to the region by addressing longstanding grievances dating back to the Nigerian Civil War. Kalu, who acknowledged the contributions of the President to the establishment of the SEDC, said the commission’s interventions would soon begin to translate into visible development across the five South-East states. He also commended the President for supporting his emergence as Deputy Speaker, describing the position as an opportunity to advance the interests of the region. item.title: Car washer steals customer’s SUV
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—A 36-year-old car washer, Pius, has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment for stealing a customer’s Toyota Lexus 330 SUV in Enugu State. The Enugu State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Daniel Ndukwe. According to the statement, Pius stole the black Lexus SUV on November 5, 2026, after it was entrusted to him by its owner for washing at Fourth Dimension, Enugu. Rather than wash and return the vehicle, the convict, a native of Ugep in Yakurr Local Government Area of Cross River State, allegedly absconded with it and fled to his hometown. Following a complaint by the vehicle’s owner, operatives of the New Haven Police Division deployed technical intelligence to track down and arrest him in Cross River State. The stolen SUV was subsequently recovered on November 11, 2026. The police said Pius was arraigned before the Enugu North Magistrate Court on November 16, 2026, on a one-count charge of stealing. He pleaded guilty to the charge and was convicted and sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment by the court. The Command commended the operatives involved in the investigation and arrest, as well as the court for the speedy dispensation of justice. It reiterated its commitment to sustaining efforts to rid Enugu State of criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents and their property. item.title: Court adjourns divorce case of Gov Yusuf, wife to Dec 15
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – An Upper Area Court sitting in the Gudu District of Abuja, yesterday, fixed December 15, to hear the divorce case involving Governor Abba Yusuf of Kano State and his estranged wife, Zainab. Trial judge, Ado Muktar, deferred hearing of the suit, to enable the parties to file and exchange the necessary processes. While the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, appeared for the governor, the plaintiff, Zainab, was represented by her lawyer, Aliyu Baba. Bature told the court that he had received service of the processes on behalf of the governor. He requested an adjournment to enable him to properly brief Governor Yusuf and his legal team on the matter. The application for an adjournment was not opposed by the plaintiff. Speaking to journalists after the proceedings, Bature said he became aware of the case after hearing reports that a matter involving the governor had been filed before the court. He said: “Since the court fixed today for mention, I came to inform the court that I had not been able to brief him on the service I collected. He will have to decide on the next course of action.” However, the Kano State commissioner urged members of the public to exercise restraint in commenting on the matter, which he described as personal and sub judice. “This is a personal matter, so, I want to exercise some level of restraint because it concerns him personally and is also before the court. We do not want to overflog an issue that is already before the court. “We have to remain very neutral in issues like this because they involve families. There are many other stories that are newsworthy, rather than focusing on sensational issues like this,” he added. Zainab, who is the second wife of Governor Yusuf, is the adopted daughter of a former governor of the state and Vice Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso. She approached the court for the dissolution of the marriage, which produced six children, over “irreconcilable differences.” The plaintiff offered to refund the dowry that was paid on her by the governor. The divorce case comes amid a prolonged political fallout between Governor Yusuf and his former political mentor, Senator Kwankwaso, who was instrumental to his ascension to power. Governor Yusuf, while addressing pensioners at the Government House in Kano on Monday, confirmed his marital issues. item.title: Courts must stop deciding election winners — Justice Adefope-Okojie
item.description: By Innocent Anaba LAGOS — FORMER Judge of the Court of Appeal, Justice Oludotun Adefope-Okojie, yesterday, warned Nigerian courts against installing candidates voters rejected through judicial rulings. She noted that “a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration.” Justice Adefope-Okojie, who retired from the bench of the Court of Appeal in 2023, also cautioned political parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates, to avoid such cases ending up in court. Speaking on the topic ‘Electoral Process in Nigeria: Managing the boundaries of judicial intervention,’ at the GAVEL International Annual Lecture, in Lagos, Justice Adefope-Okojie said: “The credibility of an electoral system depends not only on the conduct of elections but also on the existence of effective mechanisms for resolving disputes arising before, during, and after elections. “The ideal situation should be that the vote of the people should be decided at the polling unit, rather than the court of law. The contrary is, however, the prevalent situation in this country. The political parties have done immeasurable harm to the polity. “They seem incapable of abiding by their own party’s Constitution in their selection of the rightful candidates to be fielded in the election, which, contrarily, in a number of instances has boomeranged against them, with the rightfully elected but rejected candidate working for the opposing side in the actual election, out of spite. “The parties have also taken advantage of the courts’ position of not intervening in the domestic affairs of the party, to commit all manner of atrocities. “It is the flawed congresses and wrongful substitution of successful candidates by imposition of handpicked ones, and an electoral system challenged by honesty, that led to most of the litigations in the past elections. “At the actual election were accusations of ballot snatching, vote rigging, vote buying, manipulations and outright falsification of results. The resultant effect is the recourse to the courts for determination of the rightful candidate, a duty which should have been resolved at the polling booth and the rightful declaration by INEC. “The unfortunate result is that a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration. “The simplistic answer to the avoidance or reduction of judicial intervention in electoral matters is for the parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates. item.title: 2027: Don’t sacrifice Nigeria’s unity on altar of ambition, Jonathan warns politicians
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned political leaders against allowing their quest for power to tear apart Nigeria’s unity, cautioning that political intolerance, ethnic rivalry and electoral violence could plunge the country into crisis, ahead of the 2027 general elections. He expressed concern over the growing resort to political thuggery and the use of young people as instruments of violence. He also insisted that political competition must not become a threat to national cohesion and peaceful coexistence. Jonathan spoke at the third edition of the Peace and Security Conference, organised by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja, with theme, ‘’Safeguarding Peace and Strengthening Social Cohesion in a Competitive Political Environment.’’ He warned: “We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and in our states.’’ The former President also raised concerns over controversies surrounding judicial pronouncements, particularly conflicting decisions by courts of coordinate jurisdiction, and warned that they could erode public confidence in the judiciary and encourage citizens to resort to self-help. “When citizens begin to lose faith in the courts and resort to self-help, the consequences can be disastrous. The descent from a loss of confidence in institutions to anarchy is a danger we must collectively prevent,” he said. He urged political actors to respect opposing views and recognise the legitimate right of others to contest for political power, while calling on Nigerians to prioritise competence, national interest and service over prejudice and personal ambition when choosing their leaders. In his remarks, chairman of Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, threatened legal action against political parties, candidates and their supporters who engaged in violence, intimidation and inflammatory campaigns ahead of the elections. Represented by National Commissioner, May Agbamuche-Mbu, the INEC chair said competitive politics naturally involved vigorous debate, sharp differences and passionate mobilisation, but warned that these must not degenerate into violence or lawlessness. He also cautioned against harassment, intimidation and physical attacks on INEC officials and ad hoc election workers, insisting that offenders would face legal consequences. He said: “I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation, or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff, or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences.” Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfake videos and cloned voices as

item.title: 2027: APC, ADC at daggers drawn over attack on Tinubu’s convoy
item.description: ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, and African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, were yesterday locked in verbal war over last weekend’s attack on the convoy of President Bola Tinubu in Abuja. While the APC-PCC accused the opposition African Democratic Congress ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, of sponsoring the hoodlums who pelted the President’s motorcade with stones, ADC-PCC challenged the ruling party to produce evidence that the opposition party sponsored the attack. In a statement, the spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Mr Dele Alake, said the opposition parties were arming young Nigerians and sending them to disrupt the party’s rallies. “To create the false narrative of citizens’ discontent against the President, the ADC and NDC now sponsor hoodlums, arm them with cudgels and banners, and commandeer them to chant ‘Bamaiyi’ at APC campaign rallies,” the statement said. It described the mosque incident as “the latest instance of this abhorrent and anti-democratic stunt,” adding that it amounted to “the desecration of an Abuja Mosque last Friday, where these thugs were mobilised to pelt the presidential motorcade with stones.” The council said it had seen it coming, adding that “hours before the flag-off of our presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on October 24, 2026, we alerted Nigerians to the plot by opposition elements to create undue tension, sow disharmony, and introduce violence into the campaigns across the country.’’ According to the statement, the opposition parties had perfected elaborate schemes to use deepfakes, artificial-intelligence-generated images, fake news, sponsored protests, and other forms of propaganda “to manipulate public opinion and spread lies about our nation, President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress, and the processes leading to next year’s general elections.” “These unpatriotic and disingenuous plots by opposition elements have started unfolding. Their major objective is to deceive Nigerians and the international community by driving a narrative of discontent against President Tinubu”, the council said. It praised the security personnel attached to the presidential convoy for their maturity and for exercising utmost restraint in such a delicate situation. “We also commend the fatherly disposition of President Tinubu, who has since directed the Police Command in Abuja to release those detained for the infraction,” the statement said. item.title: Manufacturers urged to prioritise safety in paint production
item.description: Chemical and Allied Products PLC, CAP PLC, has said sustaining progress in eliminating lead paint in Nigeria will depend on manufacturers upholding established standards and working with regulators and other stakeholders to advance paint safety. CAP PLC received the Stakeholder Recognition Award for Contributions to Lead Paint Elimination in Nigeria in recognition of its transition to producing no-added-lead paints and its demonstrated compliance with the Standards Organisation of Nigeria’s, SON, limit of 90 parts per million of lead content. The award was presented by the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with Sustainable Research and Action for Environmental Development (SRADeV), under the aegis of the Lead Exposure Elimination Project (LEEP), during activities marking the 2026 International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week (ILPPW). The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of CAP PLC, Olalekan Aluko, said: “This recognition affirms the importance of the progress CAP PLC has made towards safer paint manufacturing. Responsible manufacturing goes beyond meeting regulatory requirements; it requires an understanding of the impact our products can have on people and the environment. We believe sustaining progress in eliminating lead paint in Nigeria will depend on manufacturers upholding these standards and working with regulators and other stakeholders to advance paint safety.” The post Manufacturers urged to prioritise safety in paint production appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NDIC urges corps members to save in insured banks
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) has urged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Anambra State to cultivate sound financial habits and ensure they save their money in banks insured by the corporation. The advice was given during a financial literacy and sensitisation seminar organised by NDIC officials at the NYSC orientation camp in Awka South Local Government Area of the state. The corporation urged the corps members to embrace what it described as a smart financial lifestyle built around earning, saving, investing and spending wisely. The Communications Manager of NDIC, Chinenye Chimezie-Amadi, advised the corps members to exercise caution when choosing where to save their money, stressing the importance of using deposit-taking institutions insured by the corporation. She urged them to develop the habit of budgeting, distinguishing between their needs and wants, and setting aside part of their earnings for emergencies and future investments. According to her, many people earn money without keeping track of how they spend it, making it difficult for them to build savings. “Our presence at the orientation camp is to help you learn a kind of life you need to live in future as you begin to make decisions for yourselves. “Some people won’t have savings, but you see them carrying expensive hairs and mobile phones. That is living a false life. We are looking at a situation where you save for emergency and for your future,” she said. Amadi urged the corps members not to dismiss the possibility of saving because of their present earnings, saying even small amounts could accumulate into substantial savings when set aside consistently. She also advised them to prioritise essential expenses before discretionary spending and develop the habit of paying themselves first by setting aside a portion of their income. On the choice of financial institutions, she warned against depositing money in unregulated schemes offering unusually high returns, urging them to verify that their banks were insured by NDIC. “Even when you have a house, you still need to set aside your house rent as a way of saving. If you do it consistently, you will be surprised at the amount you save,” she said. The NDIC Controller, Enugu Zonal Office, Mr Chidi Nwankwo, urged the corps members to acquire financial literacy skills ahead of their transition from national service into the labour market. Speaking on the topic, ‘Know Your Deposit Protection: A Practical Guide for NYSC Corps Members’, Nwankwo explained the corporation’s role in protecting depositors and outlined the applicable deposit insurance limits. He advised the corps members to confirm that any deposit-taking bank with which they intended to transact was insured by NDIC, explaining that eligible deposits were protected within the limits prescribed for different categories of financial institutions. item.title: Nvidia: ‘I’d Be Honoured To Return,’ Jensen Huang On Possible Reinstatement
item.description: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return to the position if the company’s board of directors considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest. Huang made the announcement in a statement posted on his X account on Tuesday, his first public comments since stepping down on November 12, following revelations about alleged extramarital affairs and concerns over his personal conduct. The former chief executive said he had received an outpouring of support from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers, with many urging him to return amid the company’s ongoing challenges. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang, however, acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected of the company’s leadership and expressed regret over the difficulties his actions had created for the board. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said. “I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” (FILES) Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia Corp., speaks during a news conference in Taipei on May 21, 2025. US tech giant Nvidia said on July 14 it will resume sales of its H20 artificial intelligence chips to China, after exports were halted due to US licensing curbs. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP) | I-Hwa Cheng / AFP His resignation followed reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving an executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US criminal investigation over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips in violation of American export controls. The allegations have also drawn attention to Nvidia’s role in the global artificial intelligence industry and concerns over the possible diversion of advanced US technology to China. The controversy has weighed on Nvidia’s shares, adding to uncertainty surrounding the company, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. Huang’s possible return has attracted support from prominent figures in the technology industry, including billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk and other artificial intelligence investors. An online petition calling for his reinstatement has reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures. US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s return on Monday. item.title: Presidential Election: We Were Blindsided In Lagos In 2023 – Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Raji Fashola, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was caught off guard by its defeat in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election. That outcome is one he says the party is “working tooth and nail” to avoid in 2027. Speaking in an interview on Politics Today, Fashola said the APC never anticipated losing Lagos, the political base of President Bola Tinubu, to the Labour Party candidate Peter Obi. “We were blindsided in Lagos,” Fashola said on Tuesday during an interview on Politics Today. FILE PHOTO: Former Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola. The former governor, however, argued that the result reflected the growing maturity of Nigeria’s democracy rather than a collapse of the APC’s influence in Lagos. According to him, electoral victories and defeats are part of democratic competition, and political loyalties can shift over time depending on prevailing circumstances. Drawing a football analogy, Fashola said political parties, like football clubs, do not win every match and must constantly adapt to changing realities. “In an election, sometimes you can’t win everywhere. Most times, you can’t win everywhere,” he said. Fashola explained that in previous elections, the APC had strategically redirected its efforts to regions that were becoming more receptive to the party. He suggested that a similar approach would be adopted as the ruling party prepares for the next general election. “It remains to be seen whether, as happened in 2023, Lagos flipped, whether Lagos will flip back,” he said. “And we’re working tooth and nail to ensure that we take back what we lost.” Although he said the party was blindsided in the 2023 presidential election, Fashola dismissed suggestions that Tinubu had been politically “demystified” by the defeat, insisting that opponents underestimate the President at their own risk. He maintained that the APC remains focused on convincing voters that the reforms being implemented by the Tinubu administration deserve continuity beyond 2027. The former governor, who argued that President Tinubu deserves a second term, dismissed the ideas and plans being shared by opposition candidates. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He also queried what he described as the opposition’s alternative message, asking, “What is the alternative message to what we are currently dealing with? What is the compelling message? Obi contested the 2023 presidential election, finishing third nationally behind APC candidate Tinubu and Atiku Abubakar under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). However, he defeated Tinubu in Lagos State, where he secured 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606. The APC has ruled the metropolitan state for 27 years. item.title: ‘Even A Tomato Seller Knows Strait Of Hormuz’, Fashola Blames Global Conflicts For Economic Pressures
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has defended the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that global developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East, have contributed to the cost-of-living challenges Nigerians are grappling with. Fashola, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, said Nigeria was not insulated from global economic pressures, particularly disruptions to supply chains, energy supplies and food markets. Speaking during an appearance on Politics Today, the former Minister of Works said the global economy was still recovering from the effects of the pandemic, which disrupted economic activity and production worldwide. He explained that shortages of goods following the pandemic had pushed up prices, while the Russia-Ukraine war further affected the supply of major energy and food commodities, including diesel and wheat. This aerial photograph shows boats anchored off Oman’s northern Musandam Peninsula near the Strait of Hormuz on June 27, 2026. (Photo by – / AFP Fashola also identified the ongoing conflict in the Middle East as another factor affecting global markets, particularly energy supplies and shipping costs. “It’s also important to contextualise the factors and the circumstances that have exacerbated the cost-of-living challenges,” he said. “Even the tomato seller knows the Strait of Hormuz and prices his or her goods according to replacement costs now.” ‘Helping Families In Need’ Fashola, a former Minister of Works, also backed President Tinubu for a second term, defending the administration’s response to challenges. Defending the Tinubu administration’s response to economic pressures, Fashola listed the minimum wage review, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms, and the introduction of compressed natural gas (CNG) as part of measures intended to ease the burden on Nigerians. He said the minimum wage review was one of the government’s early responses to the rising cost of living, aimed at putting more money in workers’ hands. However, he argued that increasing wages alone could not address the problem, warning that continuously injecting cash into the economy could create what he described as “hyper-demand inflation”. Fashola said the government had also sought to address some of the major expenses that reduce household disposable income, including rent, transportation, healthcare and children’s education. He identified NELFUND as one of the interventions aimed at easing financial pressure on families by supporting students’ education. “Your disposable income goes to rent, goes to transport, and goes to health care, and goes to your children’s education. And NELFUND was, okay, we will help families in need,” he said. item.title: Atiku’s fuel subsidy reversal plan not realistic — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged Atiku Abubakar to explain how he intends to fund his proposed return of fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing the plan as unrealistic. Fashola said the former vice-president had not addressed the practical difficulties that could undermine the proposal, particularly Nigeria’s inability to fully meet its crude oil production targets and persistent security problems in oil-producing areas. He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today . The former Minister of Works and Housing questioned the source of the crude oil needed to supply local refineries and support a subsidy arrangement, given the country’s production challenges. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola insisted that Atiku must demonstrate that the proposal can work rather than rely on promises to win public support. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra,” he said. He maintained that his criticism was directed at the policy and not the former vice-president personally. “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality,” he said. Fashola also questioned the consistency of Atiku’s position, noting that the former vice-president had supported subsidy removal during the 2023 presidential campaign. He said the change in position raised questions about the basis for the proposed reversal and what measures would make the policy sustainable. Fashola further argued that bringing back subsidy would involve legislative processes, as lawmakers would have to amend the existing legal framework to accommodate the policy. He wondered whether members of the National Assembly would be willing to support such a move, given its potential implications for public finances. The former governor also drew on his experience in the Buhari administration, saying subsidy payments had previously constrained the funds available to state governments. “I was in a government that was paying subsidy, and the states were not getting money. So are we going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries? Is that where you want us to go?” he asked. Atiku announced in August 2026 that he would restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027. He proposed a temporary, audited arrangement focused on petroleum products refined locally, arguing that it would help bring down fuel and transportation costs and ease the burden on households. Tinubu announced the removal of fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, as part of his administration’s economic reforms. item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s physical and mental fitness for office, saying he has seen nothing to suggest that the president is incapable of performing his duties. Fashola, a former Minister of Works and Housing, made the remarks on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he was asked whether he considered Tinubu physically fit to lead the country. “Nothing suggests to me that he’s not fit for it. Yes, he’s older. That doesn’t mean his mental capacity is gone. He’s still giving directives. And when I see him, he’s working. He’s still reading, authorising, minuting on things,” he said. The concerns resurfaced in 2026 amid renewed scrutiny of his public appearances, including videos circulated online showing him moving cautiously at some events. Asked to compare the Tinubu he knew in the early 2000s with the president he knows today, Fashola said the president had become more mature. “Well, a much more mature one, certainly, without doubt. I am not the chief of staff he employed in 2002. That’s 39 years. I was 39 then. I’m 63 now. item.title: Military aircraft crashes, 19 dead
item.description: A military transport plane crashed on Tuesday in the Siberian region of Kemerovo, killing all 19 onboard, Russian media reported, citing a statement from Moscow’s defence ministry. “An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo Region while on a scheduled flight. The plane went down in an uninhabited area. There were 19 people on board, including the crew, they all perished,” the Russian defence ministry was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS. The preliminary cause of the crash is a technical malfunction, TASS added. “A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by RIA Novosti. Kemerovo region’s governor, Ilya Seredyuk, said earlier on Telegram that there had been an “aviation incident” near the village of Yagunovo. He added that “an aircraft, which was in transit through our region, has presumably crashed”. Seredyuk posted a video from the site in which multiple fire engines and ambulances could be seen, their lights blaring in the dark. item.title: Benue Justice Commissioner resigns with immediate effect
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State, Prof. Timothy Ornguga, has resigned his appointment with immediate effect, barely one year and two months in office. The Attorney-General announced his decision in a resignation letter dated November 13, 2026, addressed to Governor Hyacinth Alia through the Secretary to the State Government, SSG. The letter, titled, “Resignation from the Appointment as Honourable Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Benue State,” formally communicated his decision to step down from the position with immediate effect. He disclosed that he had served the state for one year, two months and two weeks, expressing appreciation to Governor Alia for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to serve. The resignation letter, which bears an official receipt stamp dated November 16, 2026, stated: “I write with profound respect and deep sense of responsibility to formally tender my resignation from my appointment as the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State. The resignation is with immediate effect. Having had the privilege of serving in this esteemed capacity for the past one year, two months, and two weeks.” He further stated: “I consider it an honour to have been entrusted with the responsibility of serving our dear state and contributing in my own capacity to the administration of justice, the promotion of the rule of law and the advancement of good governance. I am sincerely grateful to Your Excellency for the confidence reposed in me and for the opportunity to serve.” Contacted, the Media of the former Justice Commissioner, Jude Ekpendu confirmed the development. Meanwhile, efforts to ascertain the circumstances surrounding his resignation were unsuccessful as the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said he was unaware of the development when contacted. item.title: FGN bonds undersubscribed by 9% in November auction
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) bond auction in November 2026 was undersubscribed by 9.5 percent , attracting a total subscription of N1.81 trillion against N2 trillion offered by the Debt Management Office, DMO. This reflects decline in investors’ demand for the Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) debt instrument. According to the November FGN Bond Auction result released by DMO , investors bid N1.81 trillion for bonds worth N2 trillion with total allotments rising by 25 percent to N1.5 trillion in November, down from N1.2 trillion allotted in October 2026. Four instruments were offered during the auction consisting 21 percent FGN March 2028 , 19.3 percent FGN April 2029, 17.94 percent FGN August 2030 and 19.89 percent FGN May 2033, with an offer of N700 billion, N250 billion, N750 billion and N300 billion respectively. Investor interest was strongest for the May 2033 bond, which attracted N766.4 billion in bids from 233 successful applicants. The bulk of allotments also went to this bond, totaling N676.6 billion. The March 2028 bond received N162.99 billion and a non competitive allotment of N50 billion while the April 2029 bond received N241.03 billion and a non competitive allotment of N30 billion. The August 2030 bond received an allotment of N336.12 billion. Clearing yields for the bonds were as follows: March 2028: 16.89 percent, while that of other bonds were 16.99 percent. The results reflect continuous declining appetite among investors for Nigerian government debt, even as allotments tightened compared with previous months. item.title: ‘The Proposal Is Not Realistic,’ Fashola Faults Atiku’s Fuel Subsidy Reversal Plan

Fashola said the proposal lacked sufficient explanation on how the country would secure the crude oil required to support domestic refineries and maintain a subsidy regime. The former Lagos State governor spoke on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he argued that Nigeria’s existing challenges with crude oil production, pipeline vandalism and insecurity raised questions about the feasibility of Atiku’s proposal. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola added that Atiku needed to explain how he intended to implement the proposal, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to assess its feasibility before deciding whether to support it. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra. Because the reality that will come then is that he will say that, ‘I didn’t know that there was not enough crude oil.’ That was what happened,” he added. ﻿ When asked whether his position was that Atiku’s proposal was feasible, Fashola replied: “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality. “In this environment, it is very easy to throw promises at people. When the rubber hits the road, reality sets in. First question is, in 2023, didn’t he see through this when he was making the promise to remove the subsidy? And that goes to a question of credibility. Those who believe at face value that promise, he will come back and tell you that, ‘Oh, I changed my mind. I didn’t think through it,’” he said. Fashola argued that restoring the subsidy would require more than a presidential declaration, noting that legislative backing would also be necessary. “Subsidy is not just about, ‘I said it.’ It will come down to the real economy, and legislators will have to repeal a law to say subsidy is now lawful. How many legislators are ready to stake their election on going back to subsidy? Those are the real issues,” he said. item.title: 2027: Weigh alternatives before rejecting Tinubu’s reforms – Fashola tells Nigerians
item.description: …Says cost-of-living crisis is global …Subsidy return will hurt federation revenue …Defends Lagos-Calabar highway By Juliet Umeh Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to weigh opposition parties’ proposals before rejecting President Bola Tinubu’s reforms, saying the country should not “abort this journey mid-term” without considering the alternatives. Fashola, a former Minister of Works, spoke on Channels Television, where he said voters should be helped to make informed choices ahead of the 2027 general election. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He acknowledged the hardship many Nigerians face but said the cost-of-living crisis was not unique to Nigeria. “Anybody who is right-thinking will concede that the cost-of-living challenge is now a global challenge,” he said, citing the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and conflicts that disrupted energy and food supplies. Fashola said: The government had introduced measures including a higher minimum wage, support for students through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and tax reforms.” He said the policies were aimed at easing pressure on households, while acknowledging that there was “a distance between policies, programmes, projects and results.” On the removal of petrol subsidy, he said a return to the policy would have consequences for government revenue and the funds available to states and local governments. “Subsidy is not just about ‘I said it, I did not say it’. It has to be paid for somewhere. One of the things that suffered because of that was the monthly receipts into the federation account.” Fashola challenged politicians proposing a return to subsidy to explain how they would fund it and what they would do differently. “I want to see rigour, I want to see detail, I want to see numbers,” he said, adding that Nigeria also needed to explain where the crude oil for subsidised supply would come from, given constraints on production. Fashola said the government deserved credit for maintaining the subsidy removal, despite the hardship it had caused. “What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on the sword and saying because the people like it, let’s bring it back,” he said. He cited the introduction of compressed natural gas, or CNG, as one of the measures aimed at reducing living costs. item.title: Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month
item.description: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday. Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6. It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024. The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance. In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver’s license suspended for five years. Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired. Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket. He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond. Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test. Days later, he said he was “stepping away” to seek treatment and focus on his health. Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour’s Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver’s license being suspended. Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. The post Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: INEC warns against attacks on staff, threatens sanctions
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack on its leadership, staff members or ad hoc workers by political supporters. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF) Peace and Security Conference. Amupitan, represented by INEC National Commissioner, Mrs May Agbamuche-Mbu, described election officials as public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty. He warned that assaulting or threatening them constitutes a direct assault on the Nigerian state and would be met with decisive legal consequences. Amupiatan also condemned the widespread incidents of political violence, intimidation and attacks on campaign convoys and party supporters recorded in some parts of the country in recent weeks. According to him, democracy can not flourish in an atmosphere of fear and bloodshed. “Let me issue a clear and unambiguous warning to all political actors, sponsors and their foot soldiers: “The law will take its full course and security agencies working alongside the commission will go after the promoters and perpetrators of violent campaigns without fear or favour. “Equally, I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,’’ he said. Amupitan reminded political parties and candidates of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, noting that sections 96 and 97 prohibit abusive language, private thugs and use of force to intimidate voters. He said that the Act raised financial penalties five-fold, imposing fines of up to five million Naira or 12 months imprisonment on individuals and up to 10 million Naira on political parties for initial breaches. The INEC chairman added that under Section 148, INEC was statutorily empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receiving case files from the police. On physical security and logistics, Amupitan said that the commission was leveraging the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to secure the electoral terrain against insurgency, banditry and communal tensions. To tackle digital misinformation on elections, he said that INEC had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department. He said that the department was established to monitor database anomalies, verify digital assets and counter deepfakes, synthetic broadcasts and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI). item.title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality — Govt
item.description: …Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123, Polytechnic rector emerges Administrator of the Year By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, claiming that the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country. The government attributed the improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare facilities and increased investment in healthcare delivery. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma. Kanu said the administration had made significant progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed. Of the renovated facilities, 123 had been functionalised to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work progressing on nine additional centres. He also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state. In another development, the Commissioner disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council. The new quota, according to him, was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13 and reflected growing confidence in the state’s investment in nursing education and healthcare manpower development. Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award. Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development and technical and professional education. He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including a student population increase of more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare. The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget. On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review. item.title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
item.description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations. According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state. In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North. A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects. Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State.
